AdjustmentCondition.description:
An adjustment condition, used by adjustment rules and adjustment plan rules.

A rule's condition may be omitted or null, which will match unconditionally.

Otherwise the **"type"** field is required and controls which other fields are required.
The following types are supported in billing adjustment rules:

Type **"dimension_equals"** evaluates whether the specified **"dimension"** contains exactly the specified **"value"**.

```
{"type":"dimension_equals", "dimension":"ProviderName", "value":"AWS"}
```

Type **"dimension_contains"** evaluates whether the specified **"dimension"** contains the specified **"value"**
anywhere within it. The match is a case-sensitive literal substring match — **"value"** is matched exactly as
given.

```
{"type":"dimension_contains", "dimension":"ProviderName", "value":"AW"}
```

Both **"dimension_equals"** and **"dimension_contains"** accept the same **"dimension"** values and are subject
to the same per-rule-type restrictions described below.

For rule types _azureReservationReallocation_, _azureSavingsPlanReallocation_, _hideCredits_, _removeAzureLicenseCosts_, _removeTax_, _reservationReallocation_, _savingsPlanReallocation_, _uncompressPricingTiers_, and _volumeDiscounts_, **"dimension"** may only be **"bill_source"**.
For rule type _supportCharge_, **"dimension"** may be **"bill_source"**, **"SubAccountId"**, or **"SubAccountName"**.
For rule types _creditMemo_ and _fixedAmount_, **"dimension"** may be **"SubAccountId"** or **"SubAccountName"**.
For other rule types, **"dimension"** may be any of most [FOCUS columns](https://focus.finops.org/focus-columns),
[Rule-Based Dimensions](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/CreatingRule-BasedDimensions.htm)
defined within your organization (names starting with **rbd\_**),
[Tag Dimensions](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Administration/TagDimensions.htm)
defined within your organization (names starting with **tag\_**),
or a few dimensions Flexera populates for you.

An empty **"value"** for **"dimension_equals"** matches dimensions with either a null or an empty string value.
**"dimension_contains"** requires a non-empty **"value"**.

Types **"and"** and **"or"** evaluate whether all or any of the conditions specified in the array **"expressions"** are true.
Type **"not"** evaluates to the opposite of the single condition specified in **"expression"**.

```
{"type":"and", "expressions":[{...}]}
```
```
{"type":"or", "expressions":[{...}]}
```
```
{"type":"not", "expression":{...}}
```

Together types **"and"**, **"or"**, and **"not"** enable complex combinations of other conditions.

dimension.description: The dimension to check the value of. Required for the 'dimension_equals' and 'dimension_contains' types.

expressions.description: the expressions that will be AND'd or OR'd together. Required for the 'and' and 'or' types.

type.description: Specifies the condition type, depending on which type is selected, other field(s) will be required.

value.description: The value that the dimension must match. Required for the 'dimension_equals' and 'dimension_contains' types.

Allocation.description: Defines the allocation strategy and the destinations that receive the reallocated costs.

destinations.description: The destinations that receive the reallocated costs.

type.description: The allocation strategy, and the discriminator for which of a destination's fields carry meaning. equalSplit distributes the pooled cost equally across the destinations. fixedPercentageSplit uses the percentage supplied for each destination, and those percentages must sum to 100. usageBasedProportionalSplit derives each destination's share from that destination's own usage when the bill runs, so the shares are not known at the time a rule is read or written. dynamicProportionateSplit splits each bill month by that month's telemetry for the single destination dimension; the rule names only the dimension, and its values and shares come from the telemetry uploads applied to it. Further strategies may be added, so consumers must tolerate a value they do not recognize.

AllocationDestination.description: A destination that receives a portion of the reallocated costs.

dimensionId.description: Unique identifier of the destination dimension.

dimensionName.description: Human-readable display name of the destination dimension.

percentage.description: The effective percentage of costs allocated to this destination. For equalSplit this is computed by the server as 100/N (where N is the number of destinations) and for fixedPercentageSplit it is the client-supplied value; in both cases all percentages sum to 100. For usageBasedProportionalSplit and dynamicProportionateSplit this field is omitted because the effective share is derived at bill run time and is not known when the rule is read.

value.description: The specific dimension value that receives costs. Empty for dynamicProportionateSplit, whose destination names only the dimension and takes its values from telemetry.

value.description: The specific dimension value that receives costs. Required for every type except dynamicProportionateSplit, where it is ignored: that type takes exactly one destination naming only the dimension, and its values come from telemetry.

CustomUsageRateSettings.description:
Configure an internally-defined unit price to rewrite select Billed Cost and Effective Cost line items.

Conditions for customUsageRate rules often examine several of the following dimensions:
- **ChargeCategory** or **PricingCategory** to differentiate between usage or discounted pricing
- **ServiceName** or **ServiceCategory** to apply to a service or category
- **SKUId** to differentiate by vendor's SKU
- **CommitmentDiscountId** to apply to selected reservations
- **ResourceId** or **ResourceType** to apply to a resource or set of resources

Tiers allow setting multiple rates by cost bracket.
The total cost captured by the rule's condition is broken up against the bounds of the tiers to calculate marginal usage within each tier.
Each tier's rate is applied to its portion of the usage, and the total replaces the original cost.

If multiple customUsageRate rules apply to the same usage record, the rules are evaluated in succession and may override preceding rules.

info.description:
With the FinOps Billing API, customers can adjust their billing data to fit their
specific needs. This flexibility supports chargebacks, reselling, and other transformations.

Invoice schedules and schedule-generated invoices support OData-style expressions
through the filter query parameter. Invoice templates retain their existing filter
grammar. Invoice lists use expressionFilter for expressions while preserving filter
as a legacy substring search. Expression and existing filters are combined with AND.

Since 1.14, a shared cost rule defined with sourceCondition returns an empty source,
and the destination of a dynamicProportionateSplit rule returns an empty value. Rules
defined with source and the other allocation types are returned as before.

The API is available at the following endpoints, dependent upon the user/tenant zone:
| Zone        | Base URL    |
| ----------- | ----------- |
| NAM         | https://api.flexera.com/finops-billing |
| EU          | https://api.flexera.eu/finops-billing  |
| APAC        | https://api.flexera.au/finops-billing  |

- id, the unique identifier of a plan

- customerIds, the list of unique identifiers of child organizations

- eq, attribute matches the value, e.g. planId eq 'c6671c74-513a-4127-b8df-81adfb65bf7f'
- in, attribute is one of the values, e.g. scheduled in ['before', 'after']

post.description:
Creates one invoice schedule covering every customer in the request. Validation applies to the whole request: if any customer is invalid the entire request fails and nothing is created.

The schedule's invoice template is selected one of three ways:

- link an existing template: isCreateTemplate=false with invoiceTemplateId set
- create one: isCreateTemplate=true with template set, and the created template's id is returned as the schedule's invoiceTemplateId
- no template: isCreateTemplate=false with neither field, and the created schedule has no invoiceTemplateId

Any other combination is rejected with 422.

Invoice numbering is optional, and the prefix is its required part. Supply invoiceNumberPrefix alone to give every invoice the schedule generates the prefix as its invoice number, with no sequence (invoiceNumberingMode prefixOnly). Supply invoiceNumberPrefix with invoiceNumberBase to give every invoice the prefix followed by the next sequence number (invoiceNumberingMode sequential). invoiceNumberBase without invoiceNumberPrefix is rejected with 400 invoice_number_prefix_required. Once set, the prefix and base cannot be changed or cleared (see update). A number is allocated only after bill-lock passes: a failed generation keeps its number and a retry reuses it. If the sequence is exhausted the whole call fails with 409 invoice_number_sequence_exhausted (not retryable) and work already completed for earlier customers is retained. The schedule's counter is retained when the schedule is soft-deleted.

patch.description:
Partially updates an invoice schedule using JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) semantics: only fields present in the request body are changed and omitted fields remain unchanged. Supports optimistic locking through If-Match.

Invoice numbering: invoiceNumberPrefix and invoiceNumberBase follow the same merge-patch rule, so omitting a field leaves it unchanged. A schedule created without numbering can have it set once through this endpoint, as long as it has not generated an invoice yet: invoiceNumberPrefix alone for prefix-only numbering, or invoiceNumberPrefix together with invoiceNumberBase for sequential numbering; invoiceNumberBase without a prefix is rejected with 400 invoice_number_prefix_required. Once the prefix, or prefix and base, is set, the two fields are frozen: a patch that carries either of them is rejected with 400 invoice_numbering_locked, whether it changes the value, clears it with "" or repeats the stored value, and whether or not an invoice was generated yet; leave both fields out to update anything else. Setting numbering on a schedule that already generated unnumbered invoices is rejected with the same error, so every invoice of a schedule carries the numbering mode it was created with.

An inactive schedule accepts exactly three fields through this endpoint: status, invoiceNumberPrefix and invoiceNumberBase. Any other field is rejected. Use the activate endpoint to reactivate it.

Setting status to inactive through this endpoint stops the schedule's future runs, exactly as the deactivate endpoint does, but it leaves endMonthYear unchanged. Use the deactivate endpoint when the schedule's end month should also be set to the current month in the schedule timezone.

post.description:
Creates invoice exports for one or more customers.

The invoice configuration can be supplied in one of four ways:

- direct fields: provide exportType, periodType, costMetric, and displayLogoWithinPdf without a template source
- existing template: provide invoiceTemplateId; omitted root configuration fields use the saved template's values
- create saved template: provide isCreateTemplate=true and template with templateName; the new template is used and its ID is returned
- one-time template: provide template without templateName and with isCreateTemplate=false (or omitted); it supplies omitted root configuration fields but is not saved

Each customer may carry an optional invoiceNumberPrefix and, with it, an optional invoiceNumber; the invoice's number is the prefix followed by the number, or the prefix alone, and the combined value must not exceed 29 characters. The prefix is the required part: an invoiceNumber without an invoiceNumberPrefix is rejected with 400 invoice_number_prefix_required. The number is immutable after creation, and duplicates are allowed. The number of a generated invoice is allocated only after bill-lock passes; a failed generation keeps its number and a retry reuses it.

Root configuration fields always override their corresponding template value when present. template cannot be combined with invoiceTemplateId. The four required root configuration fields (exportType, periodType, costMetric, displayLogoWithinPdf) are required only when neither invoiceTemplateId nor template is supplied. exportLayout is optional: PDF exports default to flatten, while nested selects the nested layout. Values are exact lowercase flatten or nested; omit exportLayout for CSV exports.

Query the orphaned-costs inventory and cross-reference stored assignments before filtering, counting, and pagination.
Eligible rows have cco_line_item_type = 'Purchase' and an originally null or empty
native SubscriptionId. chargeDescription is the exact FOCUS ChargeDescription,
not cco_line_item_type or ProductName. The line-item type is only an eligibility
filter, never an assignment selector.
Exclude matching recurring assignments regardless of discovery month, and exclude
one-time or unspecified-frequency assignments only for the matching month. Treat
null source frequencies as oneTime for assignment exclusion only. Match exact description and
frequency within organization, bill source, and billing account. A non-null mapping
productOrderId also requires the same source product order; a null or omitted
productOrderId matches any source order. Exclusion takes
effect on save, even before normalization applies the mapping. Clients cannot
disable this exclusion. Fail the request if assignment lookup is unavailable.

Omitting billSource queries all sources within the organization, month, and billing
account. Creating mappings requires a specific billSource and validates the current
eligible rows for that source and the requested month.

Display rows may be split by currency, billing profile, product order, and customer.
Selecting a description/frequency and optional productOrderId selects all eligible
matching rows in scope, including rows hidden by display filters. Other display
dimensions do not narrow the selection. Never sum different currencies.
Orderable/filterable fields are chargeDescription, chargeFrequency, billedCost,
billingProfileId, productOrderId, commitmentDiscountType, and customerId.
Pagination uses offsets over the current inventory; changes between pages can
cause rows to be skipped or repeated.

tags.description:
The FinOps Billing Audit API returns per-rule impact aggregations sourced from the bill audit dataset.

Audits are computed at the month grain only. The meaning of "month" is controlled by the request's periodType (chargePeriod or billPeriod). Access is controlled at the organization level; callers granted the audit query privilege see all data within the organization.
tags.name: Billing Audit

tags.description:
Discover Azure charges with no native subscription and map them to a destination sub-account.

Assignments match exact FOCUS ChargeDescription values within an organization, bill source,
billing account, optional charge frequency, and optional product order. A non-null
productOrderId matches only the same source order; null or omitted is a wildcard.
Recurring assignments have no bill month;
one-time and unspecified-frequency assignments apply only to their specified month. Saving configuration
does not immediately change billing data: normalization reprocessing is required.
Discovery queries are backed by the audit microservice; saved mappings are managed
by the rule-config microservice. Destination sub-accounts are selected through the
existing Cost Explorer API. Callers are responsible for selecting a destination
under the intended billing account; this API does not verify destination parentage.

Discovery requires organization-owner access. Assignment operations use the existing
billing and enterprise rule-management privileges for the corresponding operation,
including the organization-owner fallback, as credit assignments do. These endpoints
do not introduce independently grantable Azure orphan permissions.
tags.name: Billing Orphans

tags.description:
The FinOps Billing Credits APIs allow you to browse and manage vendor credits.

Managing credits includes hiding, showing (overriding other hides), and reassigning credits to other sub-accounts.
tags.name: Billing Credits

tags.description:
The Billing APIs allow you to define and edit rules that alter how your cloud bills are interpreted. Among other use cases, this supports reselling cloud services to external customers or charging back services to internal teams.

This API offers ways to manage adjustment rules, which define operations that reinterpret cloud bills. Rules are organized into four main collections:

- Enterprise Adjustment Rules: a set of rules that apply within your organization.
- Adjustment Pre-Plan Rules: rules that typically apply to a single child organization.
- Adjustment Plans: each plan is a set of rules that apply to selected child organizations.
- Adjustment Post-Plan Rules: rules that typically apply to a single child organization.

Depending on your license, you may have access to Enterprise Adjustment Rules or to the other three collections.

See
[Billing](https://docs.flexera.com/flexera/EN/Optima/TODO.htm)
for more details.

This API also exposes Invoices, Invoice Templates, Invoice Schedules, and
Invoice Schedule Invoices so customers can manage invoice generation through
the finops-billing gateway.
tags.name: Billing

tags.description: Provides read access to invoices generated by a specific invoice schedule for an organization.
tags.name: Invoice Schedule Invoices

tags.description: Invoice Schedules generate branded PDF or CSV invoices for a set of customers on a recurring monthly cadence and email them to each customer's own recipients. Each run invoices the preceding billing month. A schedule is a single record covering one or more customers. Schedules are organization-scoped. Updates and deletes support optimistic concurrency through ETag / If-Match, so a stale write is rejected with 412 Precondition Failed.
tags.name: Invoice Schedules

tags.description: Invoice Templates manage reusable invoice rendering and export settings for an organization. The service uses the existing invoice IAM privilege family and supports optimistic concurrency via ETag / If-Match.
tags.name: Invoice Templates

tags.description:
Shared cost rules let you redistribute a set of costs across multiple destinations
based on configurable allocation strategies such as equal splits, fixed-percentage splits, or
usage-based proportional splits.
Rules are evaluated in priority order (lowest priority number first). Each rule identifies
source costs via dimensions (FOCUS dimensions, custom dimensions) and
distributes them to one or more destination dimension values.
Processing unit: allocations are applied in isolation per bill connect and per bill month.
Rules do not allocate costs across different bill connects or across different bill months.
tags.name: Shared Cost Rules
